canonical_statement: For a C2 regular local parametrization x of a surface in Euclidean three-space and a C1 chosen unit normal N, the coordinate derivatives of N equal the coordinate tangent basis multiplied by minus the inverse first-fundamental-form matrix times the second-fundamental-form matrix.
domain_and_universes: U : Set (EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 2)); x N : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 2) -> EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 3); p in U; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: N has norm one on U
N is orthogonal to both coordinate derivatives of x on U
conclusion: For each coordinate i, partial_i N at p is the sum over j of (-(I^-1) * II) j i times partial_j x at p.

killed: changed local open domain to the whole plane
changed pointwise regularity to regularity at every point
removed the requirement that p belongs to U

degenerate_cases: Singular parametrizations and evaluation points outside U are excluded explicitly. No global orientability is assumed. Replacing N by -N changes both II and dN signs consistently.
